likelihood_design: The likelihood comparison reused the Probabilistic BiLSTM-Attention backbone: one bidirectional LSTM layer with 64 units, dropout 0.2 and additive temporal attention. Inputs, chronological partitions, five seeds (42, 123, 7, 2024, 99), Adam settings, batch size 32, 30-epoch cap and validation-loss early stopping (patience 10) were matched. Gaussian training used standardized targets, whereas Tobit and Bernoulli--Gamma training used precipitation in mm. Output heads, likelihood losses and target scales therefore changed together; this was not a strict single-factor experiment in which only the output distribution changed. These established probability families are alternatives within one tested network, not new forecasting methods.
dry: The main alternative-likelihood setting used dry $=0$, meaning exact-zero precipitation after the archived $10^{-6}$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ numerical-zero tolerance; every positive ERA5 target above that numerical tolerance entered the positive component. A seed-42 exploration of dry $=0$, 0.001 and 0.01 preceded expansion to the other seeds. No verifiable prespecification record was identified, and dry $=0$ did not give the best validation or test CRPS for either alternative distribution. Dry $=0.001$ has five seeds, whereas dry $=0.01$ has only seed 42. This exploration is disclosed rather than represented as an independent, prespecified choice.
scores: For the likelihood reruns, full CRPS and threshold-weighted CRPS were evaluated from the predictive CDF on all 3,939 test targets. The formal full scores use the archived numerical-integration column, not the historical 199-quantile approximation; Gaussian integration was over $[-4,8]$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ and the non-negative families over $[0,8]$~mm\,h$^{-1}$. Independent closed-form calculations differed from the full scores by at most $4.31615\times10^{-5}$~mm\,h$^{-1}$ per seed and gave the same four-decimal model means. The integration scores are not described as closed-form or mathematically exact. Conditioning a score on observed wet or upper-tail cases is retained only as a diagnostic, not as a proper criterion for ranking the full predictive distribution.
bootstrap: The likelihood comparison used paired non-circular moving blocks of 28 six-hourly samples, 5,000 replicates and resampling seed 42. The five per-case scores were averaged before applying the same resampled indices to each compared model; predictions were not averaged before scoring. Each replicate retained 141 complete blocks, giving 3,948 positions, without truncating to the original 3,939 targets. This implementation differs from a length-$n$ bootstrap and changes tail-block contributions; non-circular sampling also weights endpoints differently. Pointwise 95\% percentile intervals were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. Paired seed-$t$ intervals (five seeds, four degrees of freedom) describe training variability separately from test-sample block intervals; neither interval combines both sources of uncertainty. Only intervals matched to the archived full scores are used for full CRPS.
brier: For Brier scores, the archived wet-event code used $y>0.1$~mm\,h$^{-1}$. No test target equalled 0.1, so this event set equals $y\geq0.1$ on these 3,939 targets (854 events); this equivalence is not assumed for other datasets. Q95 remained training-derived. Coverage and mean widths were reported for central 90\% and 95\% intervals using saved quantiles; Width90 is the mean of $q_{0.95}-q_{0.05}$ and is not Width95. Negative-bound frequency is the proportion of lower 95\% bounds below zero. Raw NLL values were not used to rank continuous Gaussian densities against mixed discrete--continuous likelihoods, particularly across the different training scales.
results: In the matched likelihood reruns, full CRPS was 0.0961 for Gaussian, 0.0847 for Tobit and 0.0773~mm\,h$^{-1}$ for Bernoulli--Gamma. Relative to Gaussian, Bernoulli--Gamma reduced full CRPS by approximately 19.6\%, IS95 by 29\% and Width95 by 32\%; overall Cov95 remained similar (0.9565 versus 0.9560). Both non-negative likelihoods eliminated negative bounds by construction. Bernoulli--Gamma increased upper-tail Cov95 from 0.4941 to 0.6445, still far below 0.95; Tobit gave 0.5454. The observed upper-tail reliability deficit was therefore reduced but not resolved.
tail: Bernoulli--Gamma reduced the Q95 and 1.0~mm\,h$^{-1}$ threshold-weighted CRPS by only about 2.8\% and 1.9\%, respectively, on all test cases. Its full CRPS was lower than Tobit under both paired uncertainty summaries, but their high-threshold block intervals included zero despite seed-$t$ intervals excluding zero. The historical observed-wet and upper-tail conditional CRPS diagnostics instead ranked Bernoulli--Gamma worse than Gaussian; these outcome-conditioned diagnostics are not proper scores for the full predictive distribution. We retain this adverse result separately from the full/twCRPS comparison.
sensitivity: Tobit was more sensitive to the explored dry definitions than Bernoulli--Gamma. The dry $=0.001$ five-seed full scores are retained alongside the main setting; a matching Tobit dry-0.001 minus dry-0 full block interval was not saved and is not inferred from approximate-CRPS intervals. The dry $=0.01$ result is only a historical seed-42 exploration, not a five-seed robustness result. Historical validation CRPS did not favour dry $=0$ for either family.
discussion: An alternative precipitation-appropriate likelihood improved overall probabilistic skill and eliminated negative prediction bounds by construction, but substantial upper-tail undercoverage remained. The comparison does not isolate the likelihood family from changes in output parameterization, loss and training-target scale. It supports the tested Bernoulli--Gamma formulation within this backbone, not a general claim that it improves every architecture or rare-event diagnostic.
limits: The alternative-likelihood evidence is limited to one Probabilistic BiLSTM-Attention backbone and the original chronological test period. Target scales differed between Gaussian and the non-negative likelihoods, the dry definition lacks a verifiable prespecification record, and the dry-0.01 check has only one seed. No rolling-origin Bernoulli--Gamma test was performed; these results cannot be transferred to the 12-year Gaussian-model evaluation. The retained 3,948-position block implementation and pointwise intervals limit uncertainty interpretation. Better overall scores and non-negative support did not eliminate systematic upper-tail undercoverage.
